questions.prompt: Complete: 'My sister ______ the goats to the field every afternoon.'
questions.explanation: With 'my sister' (she), we add -s to the verb: takes.

questions.prompt: A 'zebra crossing' is the place where people can ______.
questions.explanation: A zebra crossing has black-and-white stripes where people cross the road safely.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A hill is high than a mountain.
A mountain is higher than a hill.
A mountain is more high than a hill.
A mountain is highest than a hill.
questions.explanation: Short adjective: high -> higher, used with 'than' to compare two things.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Present perfect = have/has + past participle; with 'they' use 'have painted'.

questions.prompt: Complete this diary line: 'This morning I ______ up before sunrise.'
questions.explanation: A diary describes the past, so 'wake' becomes the irregular past 'woke'.

questions.prompt: Which adverb means 0% of the time?
questions.explanation: 'Never' means an action does not happen at all, 0% of the time.

questions.prompt: To 'express' yourself means to ______.
options: say or show what you think or feel
questions.explanation: To express means to say or show what you think or feel.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Don't worry, I ______ help you carry the books.'
questions.explanation: For an offer or decision made now, use 'will' + base verb: will help.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: After 'does', the main verb has no -s: Does Kebede teach mathematics?

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Pope Gregory XIII ______ the older Julian calendar.'
questions.explanation: Regular verbs add -ed for the simple past: changed.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives friendly advice?
options: You must pay a fine now.
You should drink more water when you run.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used to give advice or a good suggestion.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'It was very hot, ______ we opened all the windows.'
questions.explanation: 'So' shows a result: it was hot, so we opened the windows.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that shows a plan already decided.
options: We are going to visit the museum on Friday.
I think she will arrive late.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' shows a plan already made: are going to visit.

questions.prompt: The word 'pollution' means ______.
questions.explanation: Pollution is dirty air, water, or land caused by smoke, gases, or waste.

questions.prompt: An animal's 'habitat' is ______.
options: the natural home where it lives
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home where an animal or plant lives.

questions.prompt: In computing, 'data' means ______.
options: information stored or used by a computer
questions.explanation: Data is information, often stored or used by a computer.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: We packed three things: water, bread, and a map.
We packed three: things water and bread.
questions.explanation: A colon introduces a list after a complete idea: 'three things: water, bread, and a map.'

questions.prompt: Put the adverb correctly: 'often'.
options: She walks often to the river.
Often she to the river walks.
She often walks to the river.
She walks to the river often.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: She often walks to the river.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about the Blue Nile.
options: The Blue Nile is the longer river here.
The Blue Nile is the most long river here.
The Blue Nile is the longest river here.
The Blue Nile is longest river here.
questions.explanation: For comparing many, use 'the' + adjective + -est: the longest.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He has taught here for ten years.
He has taught here since ten years.
He has taught here from ten years.
He taught here for ten years now.
questions.explanation: Use 'for' with a length of time: for ten years.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive: 'Farmers grow teff in the highlands.'
options: Teff grow in the highlands by farmers.
Teff is grown in the highlands by farmers.
Teff are grown in the highlands by farmers.
Teff is grow in the highlands by farmers.
questions.explanation: Present passive = is/are + past participle; 'teff' is singular, so 'is grown'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was very tiring after the journey.
I were tiring after the journey.
questions.explanation: The thing (the journey) takes the -ing adjective: tiring.

questions.prompt: Which word best shows an event that happens AFTER another?
questions.explanation: 'After that' shows the next event, one that happens after a previous one.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Drivers must to slow down near schools.
Drivers must slows down near schools.
Drivers must slow down near schools.
Drivers musts slow down near schools.
questions.explanation: A modal is followed by the base verb with no -s and no 'to': must slow down.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Last week our class ______ a story about volunteers.'
questions.explanation: 'Write' is irregular: its simple past is 'wrote'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The roads ______ wet after the heavy rain.'
questions.explanation: Plural subject 'roads' (they) takes 'were': The roads were wet.

questions.prompt: What is the comparative of 'careful'?
questions.explanation: 'Careful' has two syllables, so the comparative uses 'more': more careful.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Saba felt nervous ______ she had practised many times.'
questions.explanation: 'But' shows a contrast: nervous, but she had practised.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Did your team won the match?
Did your team win the match?
Do your team won the match?
Did your team winning the match?
questions.explanation: After 'did', the main verb returns to its base form: Did your team win?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: She has just finished her project.
She have just finished her project.
She has just finish her project.
She has just finishing her project.
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'she' = has + past participle: has just finished.

questions.prompt: Which sentence makes a simple prediction about the future?
options: I think the new park will be beautiful.
We are planting trees right now.
She is going to the market today.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used for a prediction or opinion about the future: will be beautiful.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: They sometimes clean the yard.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: Workers repair the road every year.
The road is repaired every year.
questions.explanation: Passive = be + past participle: The road is repaired every year.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Genet woke up early, fed the chickens, and then walked to school with her brother. After school, she read a book about endemic animals.' What did Genet do RIGHT AFTER feeding the chickens?
questions.explanation: The sequence word 'then' shows she walked to school right after feeding the chickens.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The Ethiopian wolf lives only in the high mountains. Because its home is shrinking, very few wolves are left today.' Why are there so few Ethiopian wolves?
questions.explanation: The passage says few are left 'because its home is shrinking'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Our club has cleaned the riverbank twice this term and collected old plastic for recycling.' What has the club done this term?
options: Cleaned the riverbank and collected plastic.
questions.explanation: The text states the club has cleaned the riverbank twice and collected plastic for recycling.
